title: TrueVault | Utah Adds to Its Privacy Law
summary: Review Utah's latest privacy law updates, including the requirements, consumer rights. Learn the requirements, business impact, and compliance steps.
body_markdown:
Utah’s governor signed[a number of bills](https://broadbandbreakfast.com/utah-enacts-tech-laws-on-youth-safety-and-data-privacy/) in March and April related to personal data, including[a minor change](https://le.utah.gov/~2025/bills/static/HB0418.html) to the[Utah Consumer Privacy Act](https://www.truevault.com/blog/utah-consumer-privacy-act) (UCPA), the state’s comprehensive data privacy law.


## Right to Correct


The UCPA amendment is straightforward. The original version of the UCPA did not grant consumers the right to correct inaccuracies in their personal data; with this new change, consumers will now have that right.


Virtually every other[U.S. state privacy law](https://www.truevault.com/blog/us-state-privacy-law-comparison) gives consumers a right to correct (with[Iowa](https://www.truevault.com/blog/iowa-consumer-data-protection-act) being the exception), so the amendment should not add much regulatory burden to businesses that are already broadly privacy-compliant. However, the bill does give businesses plenty of time to get ready, with an **effective date of July 1, 2026** .
